causal_chain: The Rust consumer workers introduced a race condition in the ingestion queue, causing delayed processing and triggering rate limit violations; this failure mode is prevented by the existing rate limiter but was not detected due to missing alert for E789 exceeding threshold 1.5x baseline; if the alert had been active, the spike would have triggered an immediate notification at 14:32 UTC.
remediation: Immediate fix: revert the Rust consumer worker deployment and re-deploy version v0.3.1 with a patch that enforces strict queue ordering; owner: Platform Engineering Lead, priority: P0, verification: confirm E789 error count drops to zero within 5 minutes of restart and validate no new spikes occur in Prometheus metrics during the next 60-minute window. Systemic prevention: implement an alert for E789 exceeding 1.5x baseline with a threshold of 30 seconds; owner: SRE Operations, priority: P1, verification: run this check against all past 24 hours of logs to ensure no prior undetected spikes exist. Residual risk: potential data skew in normalized records due to delayed processing; follow-up diagnostics not yet run to validate record integrity across the full dataset. This analysis excludes any impact on public API surface or configuration overrides, as those are governed by stability annotations and layered loading rules.
